title: 06. Memory, State & HITL: Memory in LangGraph — Complete Beginner's Guide
summary: Welcome! This notebook teaches you everything about memory in LangGraph in the simplest possible way.
objectives: What IS short-term memory in LangGraph?
What IS long-term memory in LangGraph?

sections.title: Short-Term Memory | Long-Term Memory (SQLite & MongoDB)
sections.body:
Welcome! This notebook teaches you **everything about memory** in LangGraph in the
simplest possible way.

### What you will learn
| Topic | Examples |
|---|---|
| **Short-Term Memory** | 5 hands-on examples with an LLM |
| **Long-Term Memory — SQLite** | 3 examples persisting data to a local `.db` file |
| **Long-Term Memory — MongoDB** | 3 examples persisting data to MongoDB |

### The Big Picture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     YOUR LANGGRAPH APP                          │
│                                                                 │
│  ┌──────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │   SHORT-TERM MEMORY  │    │      LONG-TERM MEMORY        │  │
│  │                      │    │                              │  │
│  │  MemorySaver         │    │  SQLite file  /  MongoDB     │  │
│  │  (lives in RAM)      │    │  (lives on disk / server)    │  │
│  │                      │    │                              │  │
│  │  One conversation    │    │  Survives restarts           │  │
│  │  (thread_id)         │    │  Shared across threads       │  │
│  └──────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

> **Think of it like this:**
> - 🧠 **Short-Term** = your brain during *one* phone call  
> - 💾 **Long-Term** = your notebook where you write things down *forever*

sections.title: Step 1 — Setup: Imports & LLM
sections.body:
Run this cell before any example. It sets up the Groq LLM and all imports.

```python
# ── Standard library ───────────────────────────────────────────
import sqlite3, json, os
from typing import TypedDict, List, Annotated, Optional
from operator import add

# ── LangGraph ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver   # short-term (RAM)
from langgraph.store.memory import InMemoryStore
from langgraph.store.base import BaseStore

# ── LangChain / Groq LLM ───────────────────────────────────────
from langchain_groq import ChatGroq
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, AIMessage, SystemMessage

# ── Display helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────
from IPython.display import Image, display

# ── Groq API key & model (already in this project) ─────────────
GROQ_API_KEY = "<REDACTED_API_KEY>"
MODEL        = "openai/gpt-oss-20b"

llm = ChatGroq(api_key=GROQ_API_KEY, model=MODEL, temperature=0.3)

print("✅ Setup complete!  LLM is ready.")
print(f"   Model : {MODEL}")
```

sections.title: What IS short-term memory in LangGraph?
sections.body:
Short-term memory = **state that is saved automatically after every node** inside one conversation.

The magic ingredient is called a **Checkpointer**.  
The simplest checkpointer is `MemorySaver` — it keeps everything in RAM.

```
First call         Second call        Third call
invoke(msg1)  -->  invoke(msg2)  -->  invoke(msg3)
     │                  │                  │
     ▼                  ▼                  ▼
[MemorySaver saves state after each call]
     │◄─ same thread_id ─►│◄─ same thread_id ─►│
```

**Key rule:** Two calls share memory ONLY when they use the **same `thread_id`**.

```python
cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "my-conversation-1"}}
app.invoke({"messages": [...]}, config=cfg)   # call 1
app.invoke({"messages": [...]}, config=cfg)   # call 2 — sees call 1's state!
```

> Different `thread_id` = completely separate memory (like a new conversation).

sections.title: Example 1 — Simple Counter *(No LLM — pure concept)
sections.body:
**Goal:** Understand how state persists across invocations.

Each time you call `invoke` with the **same** `thread_id`, the count goes up.  
With a **different** `thread_id`, the count starts from 0 again.

```
thread "user-A":  call1→count=1   call2→count=2   call3→count=3
thread "user-B":  call1→count=1
```

```python
# ── State definition ───────────────────────────────────────────
class CounterState(TypedDict):
    count: int          # this number persists between calls!

# ── Node: just add 1 ───────────────────────────────────────────
def increment(state: CounterState):
    current = state.get("count", 0)
    print(f"   [node] count was {current} → now {current + 1}")
    return {"count": current + 1}

# ── Build the graph ────────────────────────────────────────────
g = StateGraph(CounterState)
g.add_node("increment", increment)
g.add_edge(START, "increment")
g.add_edge("increment", END)

# ── Compile WITH MemorySaver (this enables short-term memory!) ─
app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

# ── Thread A: call 3 times ─────────────────────────────────────
cfg_A = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "user-A"}}
print("=== Thread user-A ===")
for i in range(3):
    app.invoke({}, config=cfg_A)

# ── Thread B: call 1 time ──────────────────────────────────────
cfg_B = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "user-B"}}
print("\n=== Thread user-B ===")
app.invoke({}, config=cfg_B)

# ── Read the saved state ───────────────────────────────────────
print("\n📊 Final counts:")
print("  user-A:", app.get_state(cfg_A).values["count"])   # → 3
print("  user-B:", app.get_state(cfg_B).values["count"])   # → 1
print("\n✅ Each thread_id has its OWN independent counter!")
```

sections.title: Example 2 — Multi-Turn Chatbot *(LLM remembers the conversation)
sections.body:
**Goal:** Build a chatbot that remembers everything you said in the same conversation.

The trick: we use `Annotated[List, add]` as the type for `messages`.  
The `add` reducer **appends** new messages instead of replacing old ones.

```
Turn 1:  user says "My name is Alice"    → LLM replies "Nice to meet you, Alice!"
Turn 2:  user says "What is my name?"    → LLM replies "Your name is Alice!"
         ↑ LLM knows this because messages are accumulated in state!
```

```python
# ── State: messages LIST accumulates (add reducer) ─────────────
class ChatState(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[List, add]   # ← 'add' means: append, not replace

# ── Chat node: sends full history to LLM ───────────────────────
def chat_node(state: ChatState):
    print(f"   [node] history has {len(state['messages'])} messages")
    response = llm.invoke(state["messages"])
    return {"messages": [response]}   # append the AI reply

# ── Build & compile ────────────────────────────────────────────
g = StateGraph(ChatState)
g.add_node("chat", chat_node)
g.add_edge(START, "chat")
g.add_edge("chat", END)
app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "chat-demo-1"}}

# ── Turn 1 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("=== Turn 1 ===")
r = app.invoke(
    {"messages": [HumanMessage("Hi! My name is Alice and I love Python.")]},
    config=cfg
)
print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:120])

# ── Turn 2 — does it remember? ─────────────────────────────────
print("\n=== Turn 2 ===")
r = app.invoke(
    {"messages": [HumanMessage("What is my name and what do I love?")]},
    config=cfg
)
print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:120])

# ── NEW thread — memory is GONE ────────────────────────────────
print("\n=== New thread (fresh memory) ===")
cfg_new = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "chat-demo-2"}}
r = app.invoke(
    {"messages": [HumanMessage("What is my name?")]},
    config=cfg_new
)
print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:120])
print("\n✅ Same thread = remembers.  New thread = starts fresh!")
```

sections.title: Example 3 — Shopping Cart Bot *(LLM + accumulating state)
sections.body:
**Goal:** A chatbot that helps you add items to a shopping cart.  
The cart **accumulates** items across multiple turns using short-term memory.

```
Turn 1: "Add 2 apples"        → cart: [apples×2]
Turn 2: "Also add milk"       → cart: [apples×2, milk×1]
Turn 3: "What's in my cart?"  → Bot reads cart from state and replies
```

```python
class CartState(TypedDict):
    messages  : Annotated[List, add]
    cart_items: List[str]        # current shopping cart (overwrites each turn)

def cart_node(state: CartState):
    cart_text = ", ".join(state["cart_items"]) if state["cart_items"] else "empty"

    # Build prompt: tell LLM what's in the cart + ask it to respond
    system = SystemMessage(
        f"You are a friendly shopping assistant.\n"
        f"Current cart: [{cart_text}]\n"
        "When the user adds items, confirm and update the cart list. "
        "Reply in 1-2 sentences."
    )
    history = [system] + state["messages"]
    response = llm.invoke(history)

    # Simple parser: extract items from the user's last message
    last_user_msg = ""
    for m in reversed(state["messages"]):
        if isinstance(m, HumanMessage):
            last_user_msg = m.content.lower()
            break

    # Keyword extraction (simple approach for demo)
    new_items = list(state["cart_items"])   # copy current cart
    keywords = ["apple","milk","bread","eggs","butter","cheese","juice","water"]
    for kw in keywords:
        if kw in last_user_msg and kw not in new_items:
            new_items.append(kw)

    return {"messages": [response], "cart_items": new_items}

# Build
g = StateGraph(CartState)
g.add_node("cart", cart_node)
g.add_edge(START, "cart")
g.add_edge("cart", END)
app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "shopping-1"}}

turns = [
    "Hi! Please add 2 apples to my cart.",
    "Also add some milk and bread.",
    "What do I have in my cart so far?",
]

for turn in turns:
    print(f"\n🛒 You: {turn}")
    r = app.invoke(
        {"messages": [HumanMessage(turn)], "cart_items": []},
        config=cfg
    )
    print(f"🤖 Bot: {r['messages'][-1].content[:150]}")
    print(f"   Cart: {r['cart_items']}")

print("\n✅ Cart state accumulates across turns using short-term memory!")
```

sections.title: Example 5 — Mood Diary *(LLM tracks your emotional journey)
sections.body:
**Goal:** As you chat, the LLM tracks your mood in the state.  
By the end of the conversation, it can give you a mood summary.

```
Turn 1: "I'm feeling great today!" → mood_log: ["happy"]
Turn 2: "Work was stressful..."    → mood_log: ["happy", "stressed"]
Turn 3: "Show me my mood today"    → LLM reads mood_log and summarises
```

```python
class MoodState(TypedDict):
    messages : Annotated[List, add]
    mood_log : List[str]        # list of detected moods (accumulates)

def mood_node(state: MoodState):
    mood_history = ", ".join(state["mood_log"]) if state["mood_log"] else "none yet"

    system = SystemMessage(
        "You are an empathetic mood-tracking assistant.\n"
        f"Mood log so far: [{mood_history}]\n"
        "For every message:\n"
        "  1. Respond warmly in 1-2 sentences.\n"
        "  2. End your reply with a line exactly like: DETECTED_MOOD: <one word>\n"
        "     (choose from: happy, sad, stressed, excited, tired, neutral, angry)\n"
        "  3. If user asks for a summary, summarise the mood_log above."
    )

    response = llm.invoke([system] + state["messages"])

    # Extract mood from reply
    new_mood_log = list(state["mood_log"])
    for line in response.content.split("\n"):
        if "DETECTED_MOOD:" in line.upper():
            mood = line.split(":")[-1].strip().lower()
            new_mood_log.append(mood)
            break

    return {"messages": [response], "mood_log": new_mood_log}

g = StateGraph(MoodState)
g.add_node("mood", mood_node)
g.add_edge(START, "mood")
g.add_edge("mood", END)
app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "mood-diary-1"}}

diary_entries = [
    "I had an amazing morning! Got lots done.",
    "Afternoon meetings drained me completely...",
    "Just finished a workout, feeling energized!",
    "Can you show me a summary of my mood today?",
]

for entry in diary_entries:
    print(f"\n📝 You: {entry}")
    r = app.invoke(
        {"messages": [HumanMessage(entry)], "mood_log": []},
        config=cfg
    )
    clean_reply = "\n".join(
        l for l in r["messages"][-1].content.split("\n")
        if "DETECTED_MOOD" not in l.upper()
    )
    print(f"🤖 Bot: {clean_reply[:200].strip()}")
    print(f"   😊 Mood log: {r['mood_log']}")

print("\n✅ Mood history accumulates in short-term memory across the whole conversation!")
```

sections.title: Short-Term Memory — Quick Recap
sections.body:
| Concept | Detail |
|---|---|
| **What stores it?** | `MemorySaver` checkpointer (in RAM) |
| **Scope** | One `thread_id` = one conversation |
| **Key reducer** | `Annotated[List, add]` for accumulating lists |
| **How to share threads?** | Use same `thread_id` in `config` |
| **How to start fresh?** | Use a new `thread_id` |

```python
# Pattern you use in ALL short-term examples:
app = graph.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())
cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "some-unique-id"}}
app.invoke({...}, config=cfg)
```

sections.title: What IS long-term memory in LangGraph?
sections.body:
Long-term memory survives:
- ✅ App restarts  
- ✅ Across different `thread_id`s  
- ✅ Days, weeks, months later

**Why SQLite?**
- Built into Python (`import sqlite3`) — no extra setup!
- Data saved to a local `.db` file on your disk
- Perfect for single-machine apps

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LangGraph Graph (with SQLite checkpointer)         │
│                                                     │
│  Thread-1 ──saves──► user_data.db ◄──reads── Thread-2 │
│  Session-A                         Session-B        │
│  (yesterday)                       (today)          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Two ways to use SQLite in LangGraph

| Approach | Use case |
|---|---|
| **SQLite as Checkpointer** | Persist *conversation state* to disk (survives restarts) |
| **SQLite as Custom Store** | Persist *user data* shared across all conversations |

sections.title: SQLite Helper — Custom Store Class
sections.body:
This is a reusable helper that gives us `put`, `get`, and `search` methods backed by a SQLite file.

```python
import sqlite3, json

class SQLiteStore:
    """
    A simple key-value store backed by SQLite.
    
    Usage:
        store = SQLiteStore("my_data.db")
        store.put(namespace=("user","alice"), key="profile", value={"age":25})
        data  = store.get(namespace=("user","alice"), key="profile")
        all_  = store.search(namespace=("user","alice"))
    """
    def __init__(self, db_path: str):
        self.db_path = db_path
        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, check_same_thread=False)
        self.conn.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS kv_store (
                namespace TEXT NOT NULL,
                key       TEXT NOT NULL,
                value     TEXT NOT NULL,
                PRIMARY KEY (namespace, key)
            )
        """)
        self.conn.commit()
        print(f"✅ SQLiteStore connected → {db_path}")

    def put(self, namespace: tuple, key: str, value: dict):
        ns = json.dumps(namespace)
        self.conn.execute(
            "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO kv_store VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (ns, key, json.dumps(value))
        )
        self.conn.commit()

    def get(self, namespace: tuple, key: str):
        ns = json.dumps(namespace)
        cur = self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT value FROM kv_store WHERE namespace=? AND key=?", (ns, key)
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
        return json.loads(row[0]) if row else None

    def search(self, namespace: tuple):
        ns = json.dumps(namespace)
        cur = self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT key, value FROM kv_store WHERE namespace=?", (ns,)
        )
        return [(row[0], json.loads(row[1])) for row in cur.fetchall()]

    def delete(self, namespace: tuple, key: str):
        ns = json.dumps(namespace)
        self.conn.execute(
            "DELETE FROM kv_store WHERE namespace=? AND key=?", (ns, key)
        )
        self.conn.commit()

    def close(self):
        self.conn.close()

# Create the shared store (will create 'langgraph_memory.db' on disk)
sqlite_store = SQLiteStore("langgraph_memory.db")
print("Database file created on disk — data will survive restarts!")
```

sections.title: Example 1 (SQLite) — User Profile Bot *(persist profile across sessions)
sections.body:
**Goal:** User tells the bot their name, age, and hobbies in Session 1.  
In Session 2 (completely new conversation), the bot still remembers them.

```
Session 1 (thread: session-A):
  User: "I'm Alice, 28 years old, I love hiking"
  Bot saves to SQLite ── "alice" → {name, age, hobbies}

Session 2 (thread: session-B):  ← totally new conversation!
  User: "What do you know about me?"
  Bot reads from SQLite → "Your name is Alice, you're 28..."
```

```python
class ProfileState(TypedDict):
    messages   : Annotated[List, add]
    user_id    : str
    profile_ops: str    # "auto" — bot decides when to save/load

def profile_bot_node(state: ProfileState, *, store=None):
    user_id = state["user_id"]

    # Load existing profile from SQLite
    existing = sqlite_store.get(("user", user_id), "profile")
    profile_text = json.dumps(existing, indent=2) if existing else "No profile saved yet."

    system = SystemMessage(
        f"You are a personal assistant for user '{user_id}'.\n"
        f"Saved profile from previous sessions:\n{profile_text}\n\n"
        "Instructions:\n"
        "1. Greet the user using their saved name if available.\n"
        "2. If user shares personal info (name/age/hobbies), confirm you'll remember it.\n"
        "3. End your reply with a JSON block like this if you learned new info:\n"
        "   SAVE_PROFILE: {\"name\": \"...\", \"age\": ..., \"hobbies\": [...]}\n"
        "   Otherwise, do NOT include SAVE_PROFILE."
    )

    response = llm.invoke([system] + state["messages"])

    # Parse and save profile if LLM detected new info
    for line in response.content.split("\n"):
        if "SAVE_PROFILE:" in line:
            try:
                json_str = line.split("SAVE_PROFILE:")[-1].strip()
                new_profile = json.loads(json_str)
                sqlite_store.put(("user", user_id), "profile", new_profile)
                print(f"   💾 Saved to SQLite: {new_profile}")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"   ⚠️  Parse error: {e}")
            break

    # Clean reply (hide SAVE_PROFILE line from user)
    clean_lines = [l for l in response.content.split("\n") if "SAVE_PROFILE" not in l]
    clean_response = AIMessage("\n".join(clean_lines).strip())

    return {"messages": [clean_response]}

# Build graph
g = StateGraph(ProfileState)
g.add_node("profile_bot", profile_bot_node)
g.add_edge(START, "profile_bot")
g.add_edge("profile_bot", END)
app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())   # short-term for THIS session

# ─── SESSION 1: User introduces themselves ─────────────────────
print("=" * 55)
print("SESSION 1 — User introduces themselves")
print("=" * 55)
cfg1 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "session-A"}}

r = app.invoke({
    "messages" : [HumanMessage("Hi! I'm Alice, 28 years old. I love hiking and reading sci-fi books.")],
    "user_id"  : "alice",
    "profile_ops": "auto"
}, config=cfg1)
print(f"Bot: {r['messages'][-1].content[:300]}\n")

# ─── SESSION 2: Completely new thread — does it remember Alice? ─
print("=" * 55)
print("SESSION 2 — New thread, but SQLite remembers Alice!")
print("=" * 55)
cfg2 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "session-B"}}   # NEW thread_id

r = app.invoke({
    "messages" : [HumanMessage("Hello! What do you know about me?")],
    "user_id"  : "alice",   # same user_id → same SQLite namespace
    "profile_ops": "auto"
}, config=cfg2)
print(f"Bot: {r['messages'][-1].content[:300]}")
print("\n✅ Profile loaded from SQLite even in a brand new thread!")
```

sections.title: Example 2 (SQLite) — Learning Progress Tracker *(cross-session study tracker)
sections.body:
**Goal:** Track which Python topics a student has studied.  
Each study session adds to their progress stored in SQLite.  
A new session can see all previous progress.

```
Session 1:  Studied "variables" and "lists"      → saved to SQLite
Session 2:  Studied "functions"                  → added to SQLite
Session 3:  "What have I learned so far?"        → reads all from SQLite
```

```python
PYTHON_TOPICS = [
    "variables", "lists", "dicts", "functions", "classes",
    "loops", "exceptions", "modules", "decorators", "generators"
]

class StudyState(TypedDict):
    messages   : Annotated[List, add]
    student_id : str

def study_bot_node(state: StudyState):
    student_id = state["student_id"]

    # Load progress from SQLite
    progress = sqlite_store.get(("student", student_id), "progress")
    studied   = progress.get("studied", []) if progress else []

    remaining = [t for t in PYTHON_TOPICS if t not in studied]
    studied_str   = ", ".join(studied)   if studied   else "nothing yet"
    remaining_str = ", ".join(remaining) if remaining else "all topics done! 🎉"

    system = SystemMessage(
        f"You are a Python tutor for student '{student_id}'.\n"
        f"Topics studied so far: {studied_str}\n"
        f"Topics remaining     : {remaining_str}\n\n"
        "When user tells you what they studied today, say 'MARK_STUDIED: topic1, topic2'\n"
        "Then explain those topics briefly.\n"
        "If user asks for progress, summarise nicely."
    )

    response = llm.invoke([system] + state["messages"])

    # Update studied topics
    for line in response.content.split("\n"):
        if "MARK_STUDIED:" in line.upper():
            new_topics = [t.strip().lower() for t in line.split(":")[-1].split(",")]
            updated = list(set(studied + [t for t in new_topics if t in PYTHON_TOPICS]))
            sqlite_store.put(("student", student_id), "progress", {"studied": updated})
            print(f"   💾 Updated progress → {updated}")
            break

    clean = AIMessage("\n".join(
        l for l in response.content.split("\n") if "MARK_STUDIED" not in l.upper()
    ).strip())
    return {"messages": [clean]}

g = StateGraph(StudyState)
g.add_node("study", study_bot_node)
g.add_edge(START, "study")
g.add_edge("study", END)
app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

# ─── Study session 1 ──────────────────────────────────────────
print("📚 STUDY SESSION 1")
cfg = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "study-s1"}}
r = app.invoke({
    "messages"  : [HumanMessage("Today I studied variables and lists. Can you explain them?")],
    "student_id": "bob"
}, config=cfg)
print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:300])

# ─── Study session 2 (new thread) ─────────────────────────────
print("\n📚 STUDY SESSION 2 (new thread)")
cfg2 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "study-s2"}}
r = app.invoke({
    "messages"  : [HumanMessage("Today I learned functions and loops!")],
    "student_id": "bob"
}, config=cfg2)
print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:300])

# ─── Progress check ───────────────────────────────────────────
print("\n📊 PROGRESS CHECK (new thread)")
cfg3 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "study-s3"}}
r = app.invoke({
    "messages"  : [HumanMessage("What topics have I studied so far?")],
    "student_id": "bob"
}, config=cfg3)
print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:300])
print("\n✅ All progress loaded from SQLite across 3 separate sessions!")
```

sections.title: Example 3 (SQLite) — Personalized Recommendation Engine *(remembers your tastes)
sections.body:
**Goal:** Recommend movies to a user.  
After each recommendation, remember which genres the user liked/disliked.  
Future sessions use that taste data to give better recommendations.

```
Session 1: User likes "action" and "sci-fi" → saved to SQLite
Session 2: Bot immediately suggests action/sci-fi movies (no need to ask again!)
```

```python
class RecoState(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[List, add]
    user_id : str

def reco_node(state: RecoState):
    user_id = state["user_id"]

    # Load taste profile
    taste = sqlite_store.get(("user", user_id), "movie_taste")
    likes    = taste.get("likes",    []) if taste else []
    dislikes = taste.get("dislikes", []) if taste else []

    system = SystemMessage(
        f"You are a movie recommendation assistant.\n"
        f"User's liked genres   : {likes    or 'unknown'}\n"
        f"User's disliked genres: {dislikes or 'unknown'}\n\n"
        "Rules:\n"
        "1. Recommend 2 movies based on known preferences.\n"
        "2. If user mentions new genre preferences, capture them like:\n"
        "   TASTE_UPDATE: likes=action,sci-fi | dislikes=horror\n"
        "3. Keep your reply friendly and under 100 words."
    )
    response = llm.invoke([system] + state["messages"])

    # Parse taste update
    for line in response.content.split("\n"):
        if "TASTE_UPDATE:" in line.upper():
            try:
                parts = line.split("TASTE_UPDATE:")[-1]
                new_likes    = likes[:]
                new_dislikes = dislikes[:]
                for part in parts.split("|"):
                    part = part.strip()
                    if part.startswith("likes="):
                        new_likes += [g.strip() for g in part[6:].split(",")]
                    elif part.startswith("dislikes="):
                        new_dislikes += [g.strip() for g in part[9:].split(",")]
                sqlite_store.put(("user", user_id), "movie_taste", {
                    "likes": list(set(new_likes)),
                    "dislikes": list(set(new_dislikes))
                })
                print(f"   💾 Taste saved → likes={new_likes}, dislikes={new_dislikes}")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"   ⚠️ {e}")
            break

    clean = AIMessage("\n".join(
        l for l in response.content.split("\n") if "TASTE_UPDATE" not in l.upper()
    ).strip())
    return {"messages": [clean]}

g = StateGraph(RecoState)
g.add_node("reco", reco_node)
g.add_edge(START, "reco")
g.add_edge("reco", END)
app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

# ─── Session 1: Tell bot your preferences ─────────────────────
print("🎬 SESSION 1 — Tell the bot your taste")
cfg1 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "reco-s1"}}
r = app.invoke({
    "messages": [HumanMessage("I love action and sci-fi movies! I hate horror.")],
    "user_id" : "carol"
}, config=cfg1)
print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:250])

# ─── Session 2: New thread — bot remembers your taste ─────────
print("\n🎬 SESSION 2 — New conversation, bot knows your taste!")
cfg2 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "reco-s2"}}
r = app.invoke({
    "messages": [HumanMessage("What movies should I watch tonight?")],
    "user_id" : "carol"
}, config=cfg2)
print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:250])
print("\n✅ Taste profile loaded from SQLite — no need to explain preferences again!")
```

sections.title: Why MongoDB?
sections.body:
MongoDB is a **NoSQL database** that stores data as JSON-like documents.  
It's perfect for LangGraph long-term memory when:

- You need to handle **large amounts of data**
- You want **cloud storage** (MongoDB Atlas — free tier!)
- Your data structure varies (flexible schema)
- You have **multiple services** reading/writing user data

```
Your LangGraph App
      │
      ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │         MongoDB Database                │
  │                                         │
  │  Collection: "users"                    │
  │  { _id: "alice", name: "Alice",         │
  │    hobbies: ["hiking"],                 │
  │    last_seen: "2024-01-15" }            │
  │                                         │
  │  Collection: "knowledge"                │
  │  { topic: "Python", notes: [...] }      │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Setup Options
| Option | Connection string |
|---|---|
| **Local MongoDB** | `mongodb://localhost:27017` |
| **MongoDB Atlas (free cloud)** | `mongodb+srv://user:pass@cluster.mongodb.net/` |

> 💡 If MongoDB is not running locally, the examples will gracefully skip with a message.

sections.title: MongoDB Connection Setup
sections.body:
Connect to MongoDB. Works with local MongoDB or MongoDB Atlas.

```python
try:
    from pymongo import MongoClient
    from pymongo.errors import ConnectionFailure
    import datetime

    # ── Change this to your MongoDB URI if needed ──────────────
    MONGO_URI = "mongodb://localhost:27017"   # local MongoDB
    # MONGO_URI = "mongodb+srv://USER:PASS@cluster.mongodb.net/"  # Atlas

    mongo_client = MongoClient(MONGO_URI, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=3000)
    mongo_client.admin.command("ping")   # test connection
    mongo_db = mongo_client["langgraph_memory"]

    print("✅ MongoDB connected!")

    print(f"   Database : langgraph_memory")
    MONGO_AVAILABLE = True

except Exception as e:

```

sections.title: Example 4 (MongoDB) — Persistent User Preferences Bot
sections.body:
**Goal:** Store user preferences (language, theme, timezone) in MongoDB.  
Works across all conversations and app restarts.

```
Session 1:  User sets preferences → saved to MongoDB users collection
Session 2:  Bot instantly knows preferences without asking
Session 3:  User updates a preference → MongoDB document updated
```

```python
if not MONGO_AVAILABLE:
    print("⏭️  Skipping Example 4 — MongoDB not available.")
else:
    prefs_col = mongo_db["user_preferences"]   # MongoDB collection

    class PrefsState(TypedDict):
        messages: Annotated[List, add]
        user_id : str

    def prefs_bot_node(state: PrefsState):
        user_id = state["user_id"]

        # Load prefs from MongoDB
        doc = prefs_col.find_one({"_id": user_id})
        prefs = {k: v for k, v in doc.items() if k != "_id"} if doc else {}
        prefs_text = json.dumps(prefs, indent=2) if prefs else "No preferences saved yet."

        system = SystemMessage(
            f"You are a personalised assistant for user '{user_id}'.\n"
            f"Current preferences:\n{prefs_text}\n\n"
            "If the user sets a preference, acknowledge it and output:\n"
            "SAVE_PREF: {\"key\": \"value\"}\n"
            "Example: SAVE_PREF: {\"language\": \"French\"}\n"
            "Keep replies under 80 words."
        )
        response = llm.invoke([system] + state["messages"])

        # Parse and save preference update to MongoDB
        for line in response.content.split("\n"):
            if "SAVE_PREF:" in line:
                try:
                    pref_json = json.loads(line.split("SAVE_PREF:")[-1].strip())
                    prefs_col.update_one(
                        {"_id": user_id},
                        {"$set": {**pref_json, "updated_at": datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}},
                        upsert=True
                    )
                    print(f"   🍃 MongoDB saved: {pref_json}")
                except Exception as ex:
                    print(f"   ⚠️ {ex}")
                break

        clean = AIMessage("\n".join(
            l for l in response.content.split("\n") if "SAVE_PREF" not in l
        ).strip())
        return {"messages": [clean]}

    g = StateGraph(PrefsState)
    g.add_node("prefs", prefs_bot_node)
    g.add_edge(START, "prefs")
    g.add_edge("prefs", END)
    app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

    # ── Session 1: Set preferences ─────────────────────────────
    print("⚙️  SESSION 1 — Set preferences")
    cfg1 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "pref-s1"}}
    r = app.invoke({
        "messages": [HumanMessage("Please set my language to French and my timezone to UTC+5:30.")],
        "user_id" : "dave"
    }, config=cfg1)
    print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:200])

    # ── Session 2: New thread — preferences auto-loaded ────────
    print("\n⚙️  SESSION 2 — New thread, prefs auto-loaded from MongoDB")
    cfg2 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "pref-s2"}}
    r = app.invoke({
        "messages": [HumanMessage("What are my current settings?")],
        "user_id" : "dave"
    }, config=cfg2)
    print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:200])
    print("\n✅ Preferences loaded from MongoDB across sessions!")
```

sections.title: Example 5 (MongoDB) — Shared Knowledge Base *(multiple users contribute)
sections.body:
**Goal:** Any user can add "knowledge cards" (facts, tips, notes) to a shared  
MongoDB collection. Every user in every session can search and read them.

```
User Alice (session A): "Add a tip about Python list comprehensions"
                        → saved to MongoDB knowledge collection

User Bob   (session B): "Show me all Python tips"
                        → reads Alice's tips from MongoDB!
```
This is truly shared, cross-user, cross-session long-term memory.

```python
if not MONGO_AVAILABLE:
    print("⏭️  Skipping Example 5 — MongoDB not available.")
else:
    kb_col = mongo_db["knowledge_base"]   # shared knowledge collection

    class KBState(TypedDict):
        messages: Annotated[List, add]
        user_id : str

    def kb_node(state: KBState):
        user_id = state["user_id"]

        # Load all knowledge cards from MongoDB
        all_cards = list(kb_col.find({}, {"_id": 0, "topic": 1, "tip": 1, "added_by": 1}))
        kb_text = "\n".join(
            f"- [{c['topic']}] {c['tip']} (by {c['added_by']})" for c in all_cards
        ) if all_cards else "Knowledge base is empty."

        system = SystemMessage(
            f"You are a collaborative knowledge base assistant. You are user '{user_id}'.\n"
            f"Current knowledge cards:\n{kb_text}\n\n"
            "When user wants to add a tip, output:\n"
            "ADD_CARD: {\"topic\": \"...\", \"tip\": \"...\"}\n"
            "When user asks to search, find relevant cards from the list above.\n"
            "Keep replies concise."
        )
        response = llm.invoke([system] + state["messages"])

        # Parse and save new knowledge card
        for line in response.content.split("\n"):
            if "ADD_CARD:" in line:
                try:
                    card = json.loads(line.split("ADD_CARD:")[-1].strip())
                    card["added_by"] = user_id
                    card["created_at"] = datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
                    kb_col.insert_one(card)
                    print(f"   🍃 MongoDB card added: {card['topic']} — by {user_id}")
                except Exception as ex:
                    print(f"   ⚠️ {ex}")
                break

        clean = AIMessage("\n".join(
            l for l in response.content.split("\n") if "ADD_CARD" not in l
        ).strip())
        return {"messages": [clean]}

    g = StateGraph(KBState)
    g.add_node("kb", kb_node)
    g.add_edge(START, "kb")
    g.add_edge("kb", END)
    app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

    # ── Alice adds tips ────────────────────────────────────────
    print("📚 Alice adds a Python tip")
    cfg_alice = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "kb-alice"}}
    r = app.invoke({
        "messages": [HumanMessage("Add a tip: Python list comprehensions are faster than for-loops for building lists.")],
        "user_id" : "alice"
    }, config=cfg_alice)
    print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:200])

    # ── Bob searches the shared knowledge base ─────────────────
    print("\n🔍 Bob searches the shared knowledge base")
    cfg_bob = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "kb-bob"}}
    r = app.invoke({
        "messages": [HumanMessage("Show me all Python tips in the knowledge base.")],
        "user_id" : "bob"
    }, config=cfg_bob)
    print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:300])
    print("\n✅ Bob sees Alice's tip! Shared across users via MongoDB!")
```

sections.title: Example 6 (MongoDB) — Personal AI Journal *(daily diary that never forgets)
sections.body:
**Goal:** Write daily journal entries through the bot.  
All entries are saved in MongoDB with timestamps.  
On any day, in any session, you can ask "What did I write last week?"

```
Day 1 entry: "Had a great meeting, launched the new feature!"
Day 2 entry: "Felt tired, but finished the documentation."
Any day:     "Summarise my recent journal entries" → reads all from MongoDB
```

```python
if not MONGO_AVAILABLE:
    print("⏭️  Skipping Example 6 — MongoDB not available.")
else:
    journal_col = mongo_db["journal"]

    class JournalState(TypedDict):
        messages: Annotated[List, add]
        user_id : str

    def journal_node(state: JournalState):
        user_id = state["user_id"]

        # Load recent entries (last 10)
        recent = list(
            journal_col.find({"user_id": user_id}, {"_id": 0})
            .sort("created_at", -1).limit(10)
        )
        entries_text = "\n".join(
            f"[{e['created_at'][:10]}] {e['entry']}" for e in reversed(recent)
        ) if recent else "No entries yet."

        system = SystemMessage(
            f"You are a personal AI journal assistant for user '{user_id}'.\n"
            f"Recent journal entries:\n{entries_text}\n\n"
            "When user writes a journal entry, save it with:\n"
            "SAVE_ENTRY: <the entry text>\n"
            "When user asks for a summary, analyse the entries above thoughtfully.\n"
            "Be warm and supportive."
        )
        response = llm.invoke([system] + state["messages"])

        # Save journal entry to MongoDB
        for line in response.content.split("\n"):
            if "SAVE_ENTRY:" in line:
                entry_text = line.split("SAVE_ENTRY:")[-1].strip()
                journal_col.insert_one({
                    "user_id"   : user_id,
                    "entry"     : entry_text,
                    "created_at": datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
                })
                print(f"   🍃 Journal entry saved to MongoDB")
                break

        clean = AIMessage("\n".join(
            l for l in response.content.split("\n") if "SAVE_ENTRY" not in l
        ).strip())
        return {"messages": [clean]}

    g = StateGraph(JournalState)
    g.add_node("journal", journal_node)
    g.add_edge(START, "journal")
    g.add_edge("journal", END)
    app = g.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

    user = "eve"

    # ── Day 1 entry ────────────────────────────────────────────
    print("📔 DAY 1 — Write journal entry")
    cfg1 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "journal-day1"}}
    r = app.invoke({
        "messages": [HumanMessage("Today I finally launched my first LangGraph project! Feeling proud and excited.")],
        "user_id" : user
    }, config=cfg1)
    print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:200])

    # ── Day 2 entry ────────────────────────────────────────────
    print("\n📔 DAY 2 — Write another entry")
    cfg2 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "journal-day2"}}
    r = app.invoke({
        "messages": [HumanMessage("Long day of debugging. Fixed 5 bugs but found 3 new ones. Part of the journey!")],
        "user_id" : user
    }, config=cfg2)
    print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:200])

    # ── Summary request ────────────────────────────────────────
    print("\n📊 Any day — Request a summary")
    cfg3 = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "journal-summary"}}
    r = app.invoke({
        "messages": [HumanMessage("Can you summarise my recent journal entries and how I seem to be feeling?")],
        "user_id" : user
    }, config=cfg3)
    print("Bot:", r["messages"][-1].content[:400])
    print("\n✅ Journal entries persist in MongoDB across days and sessions!")
```

sections.title: Memory Types at a Glance
sections.body:
```
┌──────────────────┬───────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┐
│ Feature          │ Short-Term Memory      │ Long-Term Memory             │
├──────────────────┼───────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┤
│ Storage          │ RAM (MemorySaver)      │ Disk (SQLite / MongoDB)      │
│ Scope            │ One thread_id          │ Any thread, any user         │
│ Survives restart │ ❌ No                  │ ✅ Yes                        │
│ Shared across    │ ❌ No                  │ ✅ Yes                        │
│ multiple users   │                       │                              │
│ Setup effort     │ ⭐ Very easy           │ ⭐⭐ Medium                   │
│ Best for         │ Chat history, cart,   │ User profiles, knowledge     │
│                  │ score tracking        │ base, journal, preferences   │
└──────────────────┴───────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: When to Use What?
sections.body:
| Scenario | Memory Type |
|---|---|
| Chatbot that remembers the current conversation | ✅ Short-term (MemorySaver) |
| App that remembers user name after restart | ✅ Long-term (SQLite or MongoDB) |
| Track quiz score during one session | ✅ Short-term |
| Track learning progress over months | ✅ Long-term (SQLite) |
| Shared knowledge base for all users | ✅ Long-term (MongoDB) |
| Personal diary that spans years | ✅ Long-term (MongoDB) |

sections.title: The Golden Pattern
sections.body:
```python
# SHORT-TERM ONLY
app = graph.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())

# LONG-TERM with SQLite
from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite import SqliteSaver
with SqliteSaver.from_conn_string("data.db") as ckpt:
    app = graph.compile(checkpointer=ckpt)

# LONG-TERM with MongoDB
from langgraph.checkpoint.mongodb import MongoDBSaver
with MongoDBSaver.from_conn_string("mongodb://localhost:27017") as ckpt:
    app = graph.compile(checkpointer=ckpt)

# BOTH short-term + long-term store
app = graph.compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver(), store=my_store)
```

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.body:
1. **`MemorySaver`** = RAM-only, per-thread, disappears on restart  
2. **`SqliteSaver`** = disk-based, per-thread state survives restarts  
3. **Custom SQLite Store** = cross-thread user data, Python built-in  
4. **MongoDB** = scalable, cloud-ready, multi-user shared memory  
5. **`thread_id`** = the key that separates short-term conversations  
6. **Stores** = the bridge that connects all threads to shared long-term data  

> 🚀 **You're now a LangGraph Memory Expert!**  
> Combine short-term + long-term memory to build production-grade AI agents!
